items.readme:
# XCL – Xbox Series X|S → Windows compatibility layer

[![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join%20the%20server-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/xcl)
**Discord: <https://discord.gg/xcl>**

XCL runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) game files on a Windows PC **without CPU emulation**: the game's
x64 code runs natively and XCL stands in for the console libraries the PC does not have
(`kernelx.dll`, XGameRuntime, `d3d12_xs.dll`, …) – in the spirit of Wine/Proton. The console's
GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL).

**Project state:** retail games run – Minecraft Preview and Unicorn Overlord are fully
playable, Fortnite and XDefiant work as far as each game goes without its online services;
see [Games](#games). The foundation is tested against real data from retail games
(shader packs, texture archives, movies and the console DLLs they ship). Details, measurements and
next steps:
[`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md); design: [`docs/specs/2026-11-20-xcl-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-11-20-xcl-design.md).

## Games

| Game | Package (version) | State | What works | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Minecraft Preview** | `Microsoft.MinecraftBeta` 1.18.3064.0 | ✅ | fully playable | – |
| **Unicorn Overlord** | `SEGAofAmericaInc.Pa253b0c1Y` 1.0.0.6 | ✅ | fully playable | – |
| **Fortnite** | `436609B6.FortniteClient` 2.0.1461.7919 | ✅ | works fully, as far as the game allows without its online services | the game itself is online-only (multiplayer servers) |
| **XDefiant** | `Ubisoft.XDefiant-Game` 1.0.0.186 | ✅ | works fully, as far as the game allows without its servers | the game's own servers have been shut down |
| **A newer retail game** | – | 🚧 | starts in ~4 s, runs at a steady 30 fps without a crash, shows its menus and goes on past the first one to its settings; fits a 32 GB machine (~15 GB committed in the menus) | gameplay not reached yet; its minimap mesh pipelines are refused |

## Highlights

- **100 % of a retail game's shaders translate** – all 26 698 RDNA2 programs (26 503 records) of its shader pack
  become HLSL; random samples compile to DXIL with 0 errors.
- **The game's own console DLLs run on the PC** – its Bink 2 video codec decodes the game's
  movies, its ray-tracing BVH builder builds acceleration structures on a PC GPU, the AMD FSR 4
  console upscaler runs a whole frame on a PC GPU, the GDK HTTP library initialises.
- **Console textures decode exactly** – the GFX10 tiling and mip layout reproduce 909 of 912
  textures of the game's texture archive byte for byte, its volume textures included.
- **370+ automated tests**, including GPU tests that compare translated shaders against expected
  results instruction by instruction.

## What works

✅ done and verified

### Running the game's code

| Feature | State | What it does | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PE loader** | ✅ | relocations, imports by name / ordinal / delay-load, TLS callbacks, exception tables, game DLLs, data-driven import routing (HLE / Windows / stub) | the game's 16 console DLLs load with 0 unresolved imports |
| **kernelx** | ✅ | title memory (budget from MicrosoftGame.Config, physical pages), threads on the PC's processors, modules, OS / console info | unit + end-to-end tests |
| **Memory** | ✅ | title graphics memory shared by CPU and GPU without copies, up to 16 GB (4 GiB windows) | GPU tests: loads, stores and atomics across windows |
| **File system** | ✅ | console paths (`GAME:`, `G:`, `D:` …) → the game folder; writes go to an overlay, the game folder is never modified; the console's drives: `S:\` (persistent local storage) and `T:\` (temp) in the title's data folder; free disk space answered for console paths | end-to-end: the test title's folder stays byte-identical; PLS and free space through the real call path |

### System services

| Feature | State | What it does | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **XGameRuntime** | ✅ | the GDK thunk protocol real titles use, laid out from a table of all 396 GDK runtime functions; offline XUser, XGameSave, persistent local storage, XPackage, XGame (title id), XSystem – the title sees an Xbox Series X / S; task queues, async, networking and dialogs through the PC's XGameRuntime | the game's libHttpClient initialises; users, saves and storage through the real call path; slot layout cross-checked against the game's own thunks |
| **Input** | ✅ | GameInput: one gamepad – the PC's XInput controller, and keyboard and mouse as a gamepad (see [Controls](#controls)) | unit tests; an Xbox controller in Minecraft |
| **Audio** | ✅ | XAudio2 → system XAudio2.9 (PCM / float voices; Opus 0x704F decoded via `MSOpusDecoder.dll`; XMA1 / XMA2 decoded in pure Rust) | unit + end-to-end tests |

### Graphics

| Feature | State | What it does | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Shader recompiler** | ✅ | RDNA2 → HLSL → DXIL: VS, PS, CS, mesh (NGG), GS; atomics, LDS, scratch, images, samplers incl. static ones, wave ops, ray-tracing instructions; structured control flow; parallel DXC, disk cache | 26 698 / 26 698 programs of the retail pack; 0 DXC errors on random samples; per-instruction GPU tests |
| **Pipelines** | ✅ | PSOs from console shaders: VS+PS, CS, MS+PS, VS+GS+PS; root signature with the shaders' static samplers; non-blocking creation – a pipeline whose shaders are not compiled yet gets a stand-in at once and is built in the background | GPU tests drawing the game's own VS / PS pairs, also built in the background |
| **D3D12.X compute** | ✅ | console device slots, console descriptor heaps (T# / V# / S#), buffers at their console addresses, compute command lists recorded in the console format and replayed (tables, barriers, clears, copies) | the game's BVH builder and FSR 4 record and run through XCL |
| **D3D12.X graphics** | ✅ | device, resources and heaps (also placed in title memory), pipelines; the title's graphics command lists – draws, indirect draws, graphics root arguments, barriers, copies, clears – and command lists recorded by console code, replayed; `PresentX` and frame pacing into an XCL window | Minecraft Preview plays its worlds (millions of draws, none skipped); Fortnite and XDefiant draw their screens |
| **Textures** | ✅ | GFX10 tiling (all 14 2D swizzle modes, the 6 3D thick modes, linear), mip chains with mip tail, arrays, cubes and 3D textures → PC textures | 909 / 912 retail textures exact (the 3 volume LUTs decode smooth); GPU upload bit exact |
| **Ray tracing** | ✅ | BLAS / TLAS built on the GPU by the game's own XboxBvhBuilder; RDNA2 BVH node format; BVH intersection instructions emulated in shaders | GPU traversal = brute force reference; the game's builder output checked on the GPU |
| **Upscaling** | ✅ | the game's AMD FSR 4 console DLL (`amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_xbox.dll`): context, the 29 pipelines in the console driver's own container (FSPX) translated, a frame's 20 passes recorded and run on the GPU | end-to-end with the real DLL: a 1280×720 → 1920×1080 frame on an RX 9070, the input's gradient in the output |

### Media and tools

| Feature | State | What it does | Verified by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Video** | ✅ | the game's Bink 2 console DLL decodes its movies (720p / 1080p) on the CPU; the game's own YUV → RGB display shaders (`PS_Bink…` in its pack) translate like any other. Bink's GPU-assisted mode needs no Bink-specific support: its compute shaders ship with the game and go through the recompiler too (no game seen using it yet) | a game movie decodes frame by frame, picture checked |
| **Tools** | ✅ | `xcl inspect`, `xcl run`, `xcl disasm` (RDNA2, console shader containers), `xcl shaders` (pack statistics, recompile / compile runs), `xcl rpf` | – |

## Controls

A **gamepad is recommended**: console games are made for one, and their menus and controls expect it.

- **Gamepad:** any controller Windows sees through XInput (Xbox controllers, wired or wireless) is the
  game's gamepad – buttons, sticks, triggers and rumble. It can be plugged in or out while the game runs.
- **Keyboard and mouse** work too, as a gamepad: WASD the left stick, the mouse the right stick, mouse
  buttons the triggers, the wheel the bumpers, Enter / Space A, Escape / Backspace B, arrows the D-pad,
  E / Q Y / X, Shift / Ctrl the stick clicks, Tab View, P Menu. `keyboard_mouse` and `mouse_sensitivity` in
  the game's `xcl.toml` turn it off or change the mouse speed. A gamepad and the keyboard / mouse can be
  used together.

## Building and usage

Windows 10/11 x64, Rust (`stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`), the Windows SDK (DXC: `dxcompiler.dll`
+ `dxil.dll`, looked up in `Windows Kits\10\bin\<version>\x64`, next to `xcl.exe` or in
`%XCL_DXC_DIR%`), a D3D12 GPU with Shader Model 6.6 and mesh shaders, and the system XGameRuntime
(`System32\xgameruntime.dll`, part of Windows / Gaming Services). On **Windows 10** (22H2
KB5029331+), inbox `D3D12Core.dll` stops at SM 6.5; place the Microsoft D3D12 Agility SDK
(`D3D12Core.dll`, plus `d3d12SDKLayers.dll` if using `XCL_D3D12_DEBUG=1`) in a `D3D12\` folder
next to `xcl.exe`, directly next to `xcl.exe`, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\XCL\D3D12\`, or point `%XCL_D3D12_DIR%` at it
(for `cargo test`, use `%LOCALAPPDATA%\XCL\D3D12\` or `%XCL_D3D12_DIR%`).

- **DXC:** 1.8 or newer is recommended, from the
  [DirectXShaderCompiler releases](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/releases): unpack one
  and point `XCL_DXC_DIR` at its `bin\x64`. A Windows SDK may hold an older one (the same `10.0.26100.0`
  folder has DXC 1.7.2308 or 1.8.2502, depending on the SDK's revision). DXC 1.7's DXIL was 2–2.7 times the
  size of 1.9's for translated compute programs and took an NVIDIA driver 1.4–2.2 times as long to build
  pipelines from ([#156](https://github.com/ivall/xcl/issues/156)). `xcl run` prints the DXC it loaded, and
  `report.json` has it under `dxc`.
- **GPU:** developed on AMD RDNA4. The console's geometry and NGG programs run as a compute pass plus a
  mesh pass, so a GPU without mesh shaders draws none of them. On GPUs with 32-lane waves only
  (NVIDIA) console wave64 compute, geometry and mesh programs run as two 32-lane halves that exchange
  masks and lane values ([`docs/wave64-on-wave32.md`](docs/wave64-on-wave32.md)) – slower than
  64-lane waves, most for groups of several waves; wave64 vertex and pixel shaders that read lanes 32–63
  can still differ there. Test results on other GPUs: [#42](https://github.com/ivall/xcl/issues/42).

```powershell
cargo build --release --workspace          # target\release\xcl.exe

xcl inspect D:\Game\game.exe               # the game's imports and what XCL has for them
xcl run D:\Game [-- game arguments]        # run
xcl disasm <shader.bin> [--hex]            # RDNA2 disassembler (console containers too)
xcl shaders D:\data\shaders.rpf --top 50   # pack statistics; --recomp / --compile N
xcl rpf D:\data\shaders.rpf --extract NAME --out folder
```

- **Without a command line** (xcl.exe opened from Explorer) XCL shows a small menu: *Choose a
  game…* (pick its exe or `MicrosoftGame.config`) or *Run again* (the last one). On an error the
  window stays open until Enter.
- XCL works on **unpacked** game files you own; it contains nothing for decrypting or
  circumventing DRM.
- **The game folder is never modified** – writes go to the overlay.
- Every run writes `report.json` (called stubs, unknown D3D12.X slots and interfaces, XGameRuntime
  classes asked for, shader statistics, audio formats, crash).
  `d3d12.presents` counts presentations, not visible content. With `XCL_FRAME_DUMP=N` (`N > 1`),
  the existing optional frame dumps also set `d3d12.last_frame_dump`: the latest sampled frame's
  zero-based index, source dimensions, DXGI format, sample step, sample count and `non_dark_samples`
  (decoded 8-bit R+G+B > 30). The field is `null` until a frame is sampled; `non_dark_samples` is
  `null` if its format cannot be decoded. Intermediate render-target dumps do not update it.
  Sampling uses every fourth pixel in each direction (`XCL_FRAME_DUMP_FULL=1`: every pixel).
  A coarse sample can miss detail; a non-dark sample does not establish correct rendering or gameplay.
- Title data: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\XCL\<title>\` (`%XCL_DATA_ROOT%`): `xcl.toml`, `overlay\`, `saves\`,
  `pls\` (the title's `S:\`), `temp\` (`T:\`), `cache\`, `logs\xcl.log`, `logs\report.json` (the
  previous run's: `xcl.prev.log`, `report.prev.json`).

## Tests

```powershell
.\scripts\test.ps1                         # cargo build --workspace + cargo test --workspace
```

Unit tests, an end-to-end test with our own "console title" (`tests/testtitle`) and GPU tests
(D3D12, SM 6.6; skipped without a GPU / DXC; `XCL_ADAPTER=1` or `XCL_ADAPTER=radeon` picks
another adapter than the first high-performance one, for titles too). A GPU test that cannot run on
the adapter (no GPU / DXC / wave64 / mesh shaders) passes too, but prints `SKIPPED <test>: <reason>`, and
`scripts/test.ps1` counts them at the end; `XCL_REQUIRE_GPU=wave64` (or `mesh`, or `wave64,mesh`) makes
those skips fail. Tests on real game data are opt-in through
environment variables pointing at your own files – `XCL_SAMPLE_RPF` (shader pack),
`XCL_SAMPLE_DLLS` (the game's console DLLs), `XCL_SAMPLE_TTPF` (texture archive),
`XCL_SAMPLE_BK2` (a movie), `XCL_SAMPLE_BVH4`, `XCL_SAMPLE_AWC` (a sound) – described in `HANDOFF.md`; without them those
tests pass without running anything (`scripts/test.ps1` lists the ones not set). No game data is
part of the repository.

## Licenses

**GPL-2.0-only** (`LICENSE`); third-party sources: `THIRD_PARTY.md` (including AMD's
machine-readable ISA, AMD addrlib swizzle patterns, LLVM disassembler tests, AnyPS5,
libHttpClient headers). WinDurango serves only as a reference – no code is ported from it. The
repository contains no headers or binaries from the console SDK.

items.readme:
# VIctory

Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can and on first use where it must (shaders). See
[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Status (2026-11-23)

**Not playable yet.** The title boots, runs its menus at its own 30 fps and
loads the world, where rendering fails.

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about 50 s) | works |
| The world (first mission's intro) | reached and runs with indirect draws; its title card renders, the scene after it is still dark; 0.5-1.8 s per frame |

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT.

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU can currently hang it, and
> Windows then resets the display driver (every monitor goes black for a
> moment). To look further, use a diagnostics build with
> `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1`, which renders on the software adapter.

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |
| GPU: world | Mesh pipelines, shader-written buffers, descriptor lifetimes, indirect execution (arguments clamped), pipelines made by worker threads and kept on disk | Most of the scene is still missing (untranslated shaders drop draws); frames take seconds; real queries, depth bounds, HDR and scaling are missing |
| Shaders | Console GPU code recompiled to DXIL at first use, cached on disk. Menus: all. World: mesh 8,191 of 8,506, vertex/pixel 10,617 of 12,346, compute 1,643 of 2,539 | 64-bit image atomics, merged geometry stages, the ray-tracing builder's shaders; some compute programs need a GPU with 64-lane waves |
| Textures | Console tiled layouts and detiling for the modes the title uses | Render-target metadata planes |
| Series S mode | Runs through the menus to the loading screen | The world, as above |

## Getting started

Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, a CPU with AVX2, a Direct3D 12 GPU with
shader model 6.6 (and mesh shaders for the world), Rust (pinned in
`rust-toolchain.toml`).

The title also needs several GiB of available Windows commit at startup.
Check **Committed** under **Task Manager → Performance → Memory**. If
`crashes.log` reports Windows error 1455, close other applications or increase
the Windows paging file size, then retry.

```powershell
cargo xtask install-hooks                # asset-policy check on every commit
copy victory.example.toml victory.toml   # then set your paths (outside the repo)
cargo test --workspace                   # needs no game data
cargo run -p victory -- config           # check your paths
```

Run the title:

```powershell
cargo build --release -p victory
target\release\victory.exe run <game dir>\<the title's exe> --execute
```

The window caption shows the framerate. Saves, settings and `crashes.log`
are kept under the data folder (default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\data`), derived
data under the cache folder.

Input: XInput pads. With none connected the keyboard is a pad while the
title's window has focus:

| Keys | Pad |
|------|-----|
| W A S D / I J K L | left / right stick |
| arrows | D-pad |
| Enter, Backspace, X, Y | A, B, X, Y |
| Q / E, Z / C | shoulders, triggers |
| F / H | stick clicks |
| Esc, Tab | Menu, View |

## Commands

```
victory inspect <exe|dll> [--imports] [--exports]
victory census [paths...] [--missing] [--strict]
victory lib-exports <import.lib> [--list]
victory shader-info [paths...] [--verbose] [--disasm]
victory translate [paths...] [--validate] [--pipelines] [--list] [--jobs N]
victory run <exe> [--execute] [--unimplemented trap|zero] [--strict]
            [--console series-x|series-s] [-- <title arguments>]
victory config
```

Logging: `VICTORY_LOG=victory_loader=trace,info` (a release build logs
info and above).

## Debugging

A release build has no debugging aids. Build them in with

```powershell
cargo build --profile diag -p victory --features diagnostics   # target\diag\victory.exe
```

| Variable | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `VICTORY_LOG=<target>=debug,...` | debug and trace output |
| `VICTORY_STACKS=20,60` | every thread's stack at those seconds |
| `VICTORY_WATCH=<rva>,...` | logs a title u32 when it changes |
| `VICTORY_KEYS=30:Enter,35:X` | presses keys at those seconds, focus or not |
| `VICTORY_CRASH_SAVE=<rva>:<len>,...` | saves title memory to the cache folder on a crash |
| `VICTORY_CAPTURE=<dir>` | saves presented frames (powers of two, or `VICTORY_CAPTURE_FRAMES=<list>`) |
| `VICTORY_DUMP_TARGETS=1` | with the two above, saves every render target of those frames |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_DEBUG=1` | host debug layer |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_GBV=1` | with the above, GPU-based validation (bad descriptor use reported, not faulted; slow) |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_DRED=1` | on a GPU failure, the allocation hit and the commands in flight |
| `VICTORY_SKIP_PIPELINES=<hash>,...` | omit draws and dispatches, including indirect ones, whose pipeline contains a listed 16-digit shader hash |
| `VICTORY_GPU_TIMING=1` | with the above, each list of a submission run and timed on its own; slow lists logged with their slowest commands |
| `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1` | host device on the software adapter (slow; cannot reset the driver) |
| `VICTORY_SHADER_LOOP_LIMIT=<n>` | translated shader loops stop after `n` iterations per lane instead of 2^20 (own shader cache entries); if a lower `n` makes world frames much faster, loops hitting the limit are what makes them slow |
| `VICTORY_AUDIO_CAPTURE=<file.wav>` | records what the title plays (our process only) |
| `VICTORY_XMA_DUMP=<dir>` | saves the first 32 XMA voices' context and input |

Every build appends crashes and host GPU failures to `crashes.log` in the
title's data folder.

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

items.name: fast-anything
items.description: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow: profile Python, Node or Ruby apps, port the hot functions with your coding agent, prove they behave the same.
items.readme:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.

Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of `target/`. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway. **fast-anything** finds those functions, has your coding agent port *only them* to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible.

## Install ```sh npm i -g @el4cteo/fast-anything # or: cargo install fast-anything ``` Ports are compiled with your Rust toolchain ([rustup](https://rustup.rs)). ## Use ```sh fast-anything go --agent claude -- python app.py # or: -- node app.ts / bun app.ts / deno run -A app.ts / ruby app.rb / java App.java / mvn exec:java / gradle run / go run . / php app.php / clang -O2 main.c ``` Or step by step: | command | what it does | |---|---| | `scan -- ` | profiles the app, ranks functions by time × how portable they are | | `port [id]` | records up to 500 real calls, creates a one-function Rust crate + `TASK.md` | | `verify` | release-builds the port and replays every recorded call | | `enable` / `disable` | swaps the Rust in or out (one marked block, removed byte for byte) | | `bench` | times the whole app, original vs Rust, interleaved runs | | `report` | markdown + SVG card for your PR | | `doctor` | checks Rust, your runtimes and your agents | `--agent` takes `claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin. Without it, hand `TASK.md` to whatever you use. ## Proof, not vibes

That port looked right but compared bytes instead of characters. 148 of 500 real calls caught it. On top of the recorded calls, fast-anything derives extra cases and lets the original answer them: edge cases (NaN, ±infinity, -0.0, zero and ±1, non-ASCII text, empty and up to 16× bigger inputs) and shrunk inputs (tiny and random slices). Nothing is enabled until every case matches: same values (floats within 1e-9), errors where the original errors. A port that is right but slower per call than the original (calling into Rust costs more than the work saved) isn't enabled either. `FAST_ANYTHING_DISABLE=1` runs the original any time. ## Results Real runs on an i5-10500, Windows 11 (C and C++: a 4-core GitHub Actions Linux runner). Reproduce them from [`examples/`](examples). | app | before | after | |---|---|---| | Python fuzzy dedupe (700 names) | 4.91s | **42ms, 116×** | | TypeScript fuzzy dedupe (2,000 names) | 3.11s | **155ms, 20×** | | PHP fuzzy dedupe (600 names) | 2.94s | **53ms, 55×** | | Go fuzzy dedupe (3,000 names) | 3.02s | **144ms, 21×** | | Ruby fuzzy dedupe (400 names) | 3.13s | **228ms, 14×** | | C# fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 4.03s | **312ms, 13×** | | Java fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 3.50s | **1.18s, 3×** (11× on the function; the rest is JVM startup) | | C mandelbrot (8 zoom levels) | 431ms | **127ms, 3.4×** | | C++ fuzzy dedupe (6,000 names) | 3.02s | **1.09s, 2.7×** | fast-anything ports the outermost loop it can, not the tiny function called inside it, so the app crosses into Rust once instead of millions of times. Porting only the inner `levenshtein` gave 35× and 1.9×. ## Why not rewrite it all? - **Compile time**: each port is a one-function crate. Seconds, not minutes. - **Cache**: every port shares one `.fast/target`. Delete it whenever you like. - **Risk**: your code stays as it is. Rust is opt-in per function, checked against real behavior. ## Agents - **Claude Code plugin**: `/plugin marketplace add EL4CTEO/fast-anything`, then `/plugin install fast-anything@fast-anything` and `/fast-anything:fast python app.py` - **MCP server** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…), built into the binary: `claude mcp add fast-anything -- fast-anything mcp`. 8 tools: `fast_scan`, `fast_port`, `fast_verify`, `fast_enable`, `fast_disable`, `fast_bench`, `fast_report`, `fast_status`. - **Skill**: [`skills/fast-anything`](skills/fast-anything/SKILL.md) teaches any agent the loop. ## Languages | language | binding | status | |---|---|---| | Python 3.10+ | PyO3 | ✅ | | JavaScript / TypeScript (Node 22+, Bun, Deno 2+: `bun app.ts`, `deno run -A app.ts`) | napi-rs | ✅ | | Ruby 3.3+ | C ABI + JSON, through Ruby's built-in Fiddle | ✅ | | Java 22+ (`java App.java`, Maven, Gradle) | the same C bridge, through the FFM API | ✅ | | Kotlin/JVM (Gradle, `src/main/kotlin`, JDK 22+) | the Java bridge; top-level functions, `object` and companion members, extension functions | ✅ | | Go 1.22+ (`go run .`) | the same C bridge, through the Windows loader or dlopen (cgo) | ✅ | | PHP 8.1+ (`php app.php`) | the same C bridge, through PHP's FFI extension (`extension=ffi`) | ✅ | | C and C++ (gcc, clang or Intel oneAPI icx/icpx: `clang -O2 main.c lib.c`) | the same C bridge, through LoadLibrary or dlopen | ✅ | | C# / .NET 8+ (`dotnet run -c Release`) | the same C bridge, through NativeLibrary; profiled with EventPipe, nothing to install | ✅ | It ports top-level, deterministic functions that take plain data (numbers, strings, lists, dicts, typed arrays…), including ones in your entry script when its main code sits under `if __name__ == "__main__":` (or `if __FILE__ == $0`, or `if (import.meta.main)` / `if (require.main === module)`). In Python that means module-level functions and `@staticmethod`s (dataclasses, NamedTuples and numeric NumPy arrays count as plain data), in Java, C# and PHP static methods (and PHP functions), in Go plain functions, in C and C++ free functions and static methods. `scan` says why anything else can't move yet. With Intel oneAPI on Windows, run fast-anything from a shell where `setvars.bat` ran (it sets up the linker). SYCL kernels run on the device and aren't ported; with `-fsycl`, only host functions are profiled and ported. Ruby, Java, Go, PHP, C, C++ and C# need no headers, bindings or extra tools: the port is a plain Rust library with one C entry point taking and returning JSON, and fast-anything replays the recorded calls against it directly. Any language that can call C can use that bridge. ## License MIT

items.readme:
# NeonClipping

**Paste a link. Get captioned 9:16 clips in about two minutes. Free, local, open-source.**

NeonClipping turns long YouTube / Twitch / Kick videos (or your own MP4) into vertical, captioned clips with a title and hook for each. Everything runs on your machine: no account, no subscription, no upload.

[![Star on GitHub](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/iamajmeena/neonclipping?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Star%20on%20GitHub)](https://github.com/iamajmeena/neonclipping) [![Instagram](https://img.shields.io/badge/Follow-%40iamajmeena-E4405F?style=for-the-badge&logo=instagram&logoColor=white)](https://www.instagram.com/iamajmeena/)

🌐 **Website with one-click Windows setup:** <https://iamajmeena.github.io/neonclipping/>

**Made by [Ajay K Meena](https://www.instagram.com/iamajmeena/)** (Director, DOP, colorist, DaVinci Resolve educator, Jaipur). If NeonClipping saves you time, please ⭐ star the repo and follow [@iamajmeena](https://www.instagram.com/iamajmeena/) on Instagram.

![demo](docs/demo.gif)

![UI](docs/neonclipping-ui.jpg)

📘 **Guides (Hindi + English, PDF):** [docs/NeonClipping-Guide-EN-HI.pdf](docs/NeonClipping-Guide-EN-HI.pdf)  
🤖 **Let an AI agent install it for you:** copy [docs/NEONCLIPPING-AGENT-SETUP-PROMPT.txt](docs/NEONCLIPPING-AGENT-SETUP-PROMPT.txt) into Claude Code, Codex CLI or Cursor.

## How it finds good moments

Two modes, one button.

**⚡ Fast mode (default, videos over 10 min)** copies the trick that makes the fastest clippers fast: never look at the whole video.

1. Download **audio only** (79 MB for an 85-minute video, about 10 s).
2. Take the transcript for free from YouTube's own captions (word-timed). No speech model needed. For other sources a local Whisper model is used as the fallback.
3. Score the whole audio track for *sudden loudness jumps* (vs a 2-minute local baseline), *raised voices* (2–4 kHz energy) and quiet-to-loud transitions.
4. Take the best moments, read each one's transcript with a local LLM (Ollama) and let it score the moment, write a title and a hook. Snap the start and end to sentence boundaries inside your Min/Max length.
5. Download **only the chosen sections** of the video (not the whole file), trim exactly by matching their sound to the audio track, and render 1080x1920 clips with burned-in captions.

**🔬 Deep mode** downloads the whole video, adds optical-flow motion (OpenCV Farneback: fast objects, impacts, camera whips) and cut density to the audio signals, shortlists 4× more candidates and gives the LLM 15 seconds of context before and after each one.

Measured on one machine (RTX 2060, 16 threads), Fast mode, 3 clips each:

| Source | Time |
|---|---|
| 85-minute YouTube stream (YouTube captions) | **97 s** |
| 3-hour Twitch VOD (no captions, local speech model) | **136 s** |
| 90-second YouTube trailer | 21 s |
| 90-second local MP4 | 14 s |

Your numbers depend on network and CPU.

## How it decides what is a good moment

Every candidate moment is scored from several signals, then the best ones are kept:

| Signal | What it looks for |
|---|---|
| Loudness jump | A sudden boom or shout compared with the last two minutes |
| Raised voice | Energy in the 2–4 kHz band (screaming, yelling) |
| What is said | "oh my god", "oh shit", "run", "police", "bhaago", "arre yaar" and similar (English, Hinglish, Hindi) |
| On-screen action | Fast motion (optical flow), explosion-like flashes, red/blue light flicker, scene cuts |
| AI score | A small local LLM reads the transcript: emotion, punchline, payoff |

**It learns from you.** Under every clip there are 5 stars. Your ratings stay on your computer (`data/feedback.jsonl`). After 8 ratings the weights of the signals above are re-fitted (ridge regression pulled toward the defaults, blended in gradually), so a gamer-shouting-heavy taste ranks shouting higher and a calm-explainer taste ranks it lower. Nothing is uploaded.

## Features

- One-click **Make clips**, live progress, clips appear one by one with preview and MP4 download.
- **Min / Max clip length** (e.g. 30–80 s). Clips end on a sentence.
- **Facecam position presets** (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, bottom-centre, none) for the usual streamer layouts, remembered between sessions. Or draw the face and gameplay boxes yourself in the editor.
- **11 native layouts:** camera above/below gameplay, blurred fill, full-screen crop, gameplay only, four corner overlays, circle facecam and side-by-side. Independent face/game selection and a face-size slider. Preview-only platform safe zones.
- Caption styles: GTA Neon, Impact, Clean, Hormozi and MrBeast. Word-timed, editable words, SRT export.
- **Hinglish captions**: Hindi speech is written in English letters ("kya haal hai bhai") by default. Pick Hinglish / हिंदी / English explicitly if you like. Caption accuracy: Fast, Accurate (Whisper large-v3-turbo, default) or Best Hindi (large-v3, much slower on small GPUs).
- **Make clips uses your own setup**: facecam preset or the boxes you draw in step 03.
- Optical-flow motion + audio highlight ranking, frame-accurate NVENC export (falls back to x264).
- Nothing leaves your computer. The server binds to `127.0.0.1` only.

## Change clips after generating them

![Saved clip editor with eleven layouts](docs/saved-clip-editor.jpg)

Open **My clips → Edit clip**. The saved editor includes all **11 speaker position/shape layouts**, a speaker-size slider, editable subtitle words, caption style and caption height.

- **Apply to this clip** updates the opened clip.
- **Apply to this video's clips** updates the currently saved clips associated with the same source URL. Each keeps its own timestamps, transcript, title and hook. New clips still being generated are not included in that snapshot.
- Source download, highlight discovery and speech recognition are **not repeated**. Burned-in captions and framing require encoding a new final MP4.
- Original source files must remain in `data/`. Previous MP4s are kept; the library displays the latest versions. Old exports missing saved word timings can recover captions from their SRT, with approximate per-word timing.
- This edits the selected moments; changing the clip's start/end or spoken language requires a separate trim/transcription workflow.

Validation on one 796.9-second source: all 11 layouts and five caption styles exported with audio and decoded successfully. A seven-clip layout/style update took 119.58 seconds while reusing each clip's exact source, range and word list. These are local checks, not guaranteed runtimes or a caption-quality benchmark.

Run the portable regression tests with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

## Install

**Easiest (Windows):** download [`NeonClipping-Setup.bat`](https://github.com/iamajmeena/neonclipping/releases/latest/download/NeonClipping-Setup.bat) from the [website](https://iamajmeena.github.io/neonclipping/) or the Releases page and double-click it. It checks your PC, installs Python and FFmpeg if missing, installs NeonClipping into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NeonClipping`, creates a Desktop shortcut and opens the app. Mac/Linux: `install.sh` (new, not yet tested on a real Mac). Or follow the steps below.

Requirements: Python 3.10+, FFmpeg on PATH. Optional but recommended: [Ollama](https://ollama.com) with `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` for AI titles, hooks and scores (without it clips are picked by the audio/motion score), and an NVIDIA GPU for NVENC and faster-whisper.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/iamajmeena/neonclipping
cd neonclipping
# Windows
./run.ps1
# Linux / macOS
./run.sh
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8770>, paste a link, press **⚡ Make clips**.

Optional GPU speech model support (only used when a video has no YouTube captions):

```bash
.venv/bin/pip install nvidia-cublas-cu12 "nvidia-cudnn-cu12==9.*"
```

Set `NEONCLIPPING_CPU=1` to force CPU. Set `NEONCLIPPING_PORT=9000` to use another port.

## How it is built

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| `app.py` | FastAPI server, `/make` pipeline, export, library |
| `smart.py` | Moment scoring: transcript + local LLM, sentence snapping |
| `highlights.py` | Audio-jump / shout / optical-flow / cut ranking, parallel decode |
| `captions_yt.py` | YouTube word-timed captions (json3) parser |
| `captions.py` | Local Whisper (GPU first, CPU fallback), ASS/SRT styles |
| `translit.py` | Devanagari → Hinglish (word by word, keeps timings) |
| `standalone.py`, `previews.py` | Link import, early preview frames |

## Live clipping (while the stream is on)

Paste a Twitch channel link or a YouTube Live link into the **Live clipping** panel and press Start. NeonClipping records the stream (Streamlink), reads chat anonymously, counts messages in 10 s buckets and cuts a clip around every chat spike (chat velocity more than 2.5 sigma and 2.5x the 5-minute baseline). The clip starts about 24 s *before* the spike, because chat reacts after the moment. It then gets captions, a hook and title, your layout and facecam boxes, and a viral score like any other clip. **Clip the last 30 s now** cuts on demand, **Stop** ends the session. It only works while the stream is live; for finished videos use Make clips.

There is also a command-line version in `live/live_clip.py`.

## Creators (clip a streamer automatically)

Add a Twitch name or a Twitch / YouTube channel link in the **Creators** panel. NeonClipping checks every minute; when that creator goes live it records the stream and clips the chat spikes, using the layout, facecam boxes and caption style you had selected when you added them (“Use my current layout” updates it). Clips appear under the creator and in My clips.

- One stream at a time (recording and rendering are heavy); other creators wait their turn.
- NeonClipping must stay open. Unattended recordings stop after 3 hours (a new one starts if the creator is still live), stop when less than 8 GB of disk is free, and the big recording file is deleted after the last clip is cut.
- Pressing **Stop** pauses that creator for 30 minutes; switching Auto off and on resumes at once.
- Tested on Twitch (recording, chat spikes, clip, feed). YouTube channels are detected through yt-dlp; an auto-clipped YouTube stream was not run end to end.

## Tests

`tests/` holds an end-to-end suite that runs against the live server: page and API validation, every layout and caption style rendered and measured, editing one / all clips of a video, Make clips on real YouTube / Twitch / local sources in every mode and language, live clipping on a real stream, the creator list, star ratings, the installer and the website. Unit tests cover the chat-spike rule, caption grouping and re-editing. The last full run is in [`tests/REPORT.md`](tests/REPORT.md): 187 checks, all passing, plus the 12 problems the run found and fixed.

```
python -m unittest tests.test_captions tests.test_live tests.test_reedit
python tests/e2e.py static export edit creators feedback   # server must be running
python tests/e2e_make.py          # real downloads + transcription (about 25 min)
python tests/e2e_live.py          # needs a Twitch channel that is live
python tests/e2e_site.py          # website, links, release assets
python tests/make_report.py       # rebuild tests/REPORT.md
```

## Style & extras

- **Templates:** wrap the clip in an *X post* (light or dark), a *TikTok hook* box or a *Breaking news* broadcast frame. Type the name, handle and hook; the card, avatar letter, check mark and ticker are drawn for you.
- **Background card:** padded, rounded-corner video card on a blurred copy, a colour, a gradient or your own image (dimmed, blurred).
- **Logo / watermark** (4 corners, size, opacity), **credit line** (or "Clip: channel name" automatically), **outro ribbon** that slides in for the last seconds.
- **Music bed:** one track under the voice that rises to a peak volume in the last seconds (volume, peak and riser length are yours).
- **Six caption animations:** highlight (word by word), pop-in, pop-in line, one by one, build up, full line.
- **Import captions:** drop an `.srt` or `.ass` file; the words are timed to the clip and can be edited.
- All of it works in Make clips, single exports and "Edit saved clips" (including "apply to all clips of this video").

## Find my facecam

The **Find my facecam** chip (or "find it automatically when I press Make clips") looks at 14 frames of the video, finds rectangles whose border stays in the same place, and keeps the one that holds a face (small local YuNet face model, MIT licence, `models/`). It rejects the game's minimap and HUD panels, finds webcams in a corner or floating on a side, and answers "no facecam" when it is not sure. Measured on 30 real saved streams: found the webcam on every stream that has one; clean "not found" on trailers and talking-head videos. Not perfect: some boxes cover only the face inside a framed webcam.

## Long streams with a free chatbot

**AI parts** (below step 01): paste a YouTube link, NeonClipping splits the video's captions into ~25-minute parts and gives a copy-ready prompt per part. Paste each into any free chatbot, paste all answers back (JSON or lines like `12:30-13:10 title`), tick the moments and press Make clips: only those sections are downloaded and rendered. A chatbot given a 9-hour transcript in one go only reads the start; small parts fix that. Nothing is sent anywhere by NeonClipping; the chatbot step is manual.

## Honest limits

- Highlight picking is a heuristic plus a small local LLM. It finds loud, energetic, quotable moments, not guaranteed "viral" ones. Review before posting.
- The action cues (motion, flash, light flicker) are simple heuristics on a tiny low-resolution copy; they rank moments, they do not recognise "a police chase". Star ratings are how it gets better at your taste.
- The LLM sees text only. It cannot see the screen.
- Without YouTube captions (Twitch VODs, uploaded files) a speech model must transcribe each candidate, which is slow on CPU.
- Auto-caption accuracy follows the source: YouTube's auto captions are imperfect, especially Hinglish.
- Deep mode was verified on a short video only; on multi-hour videos it downloads the whole file first and is slow by design.
- Facecam presets are starting points, not detection: if you pick Bottom-right but the cam is bottom-left, the top half of the clip will show the wrong area. Pick the right corner or draw your own boxes.

## Support

NeonClipping is free. If it saves you time you can ⭐ star the repo, follow [@iamajmeena](https://www.instagram.com/iamajmeena/), or optionally donate via Razorpay (UPI / cards): <https://rzp.io/rzp/JN41CpW>. The app also has a ♥ Donate button. Nothing is ever locked behind a donation.

## Credits and inspiration

Design ideas studied from open-source clippers: [PeakCut](https://github.com/haziqahmedqasmi/PeakCut) (audio-first download, captions as transcript, section download), [ClipCutter](https://github.com/curtyo18/ClipCutter), [content-ai](https://github.com/buddah0/content-ai), and the Growlance live-clipper script. Also studied: PeakCut's facecam-by-static-border idea and creator list (reimplemented here with our own code, plus a face check), the public feature list of the YIZERGE desktop editor (templates, background card, music riser, caption animations; only its public web page was read), and a creator's walkthrough of splitting a 9-hour stream into small transcript parts for a free chatbot. Built on FFmpeg, yt-dlp, FastAPI, faster-whisper, OpenCV (YuNet face detector, MIT), Ollama.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

items.readme:
# xnulinux

Run macOS userspace on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it.

xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source kernel of macOS, from Apple's published sources and runs it as a loadable kernel
module (`xnu.ko`) inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS
processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its
memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module (`fki.ko`).

With a stock Ubuntu kernel, `insmod xnu.ko` boots a macOS 27 system disk made by Apple's own installer to the
desktop: loginwindow, WindowServer, Dock, Finder, Safari and Chrome.

![macOS and Linux userspace side by side](docs/images/macos-and-linux.jpg)

*One system, two userspaces. Left: a Terminal in the hosted macOS 27.2.1 (`sw_vers`, the Darwin kernel, launchd,
WindowServer, Dock and Finder running). Right: from that macOS, an SSH session into the Linux it runs inside (Ubuntu,
Linux 7.0, the `xnu` and `fki` modules loaded, and the `insmod xnu.ko` process the macOS kernel runs in).
Straight from the hosted framebuffer, 1280×800.*

![The hosted macOS desktop](docs/images/desktop.jpg)

*The hosted desktop at the end of a 30-minute stress run, rendered on the CPU (no GPU bridge).*

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Safari on Wikipedia's XNU article](docs/images/safari-xnu.jpg) | ![Safari on kernel.org](docs/images/safari-kernel-org.jpg) |
| ![Safari on GitHub](docs/images/safari-github.jpg) | |

*Safari in the hosted macOS: Wikipedia's article on XNU, kernel.org and the Linux repository on GitHub, over the
hosted system's network link through Linux, with the GPU bridge on (`GPU=auto`).*

![Hosted macOS running on bare-metal NVIDIA DGX Spark](docs/images/dgx-spark.jpg)

*Bare-metal NVIDIA DGX Spark (Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS aarch64, Linux `7.0.0-1025-nvidia`): hosted macOS 27 running with
4 CPUs and 8 GiB of RAM (CPU rendering), shown over macOS Screen Sharing alongside an SSH session from the DGX Spark
host into the hosted Darwin userspace.*

![About This Mac and sysctl on bare-metal NVIDIA DGX Spark](docs/images/dgx-spark-about.jpg)

*Inside the hosted macOS on DGX Spark: About This Mac (`Chip: Unknown`, `7.80 GB` memory, `macOS Golden Gate 27.2`)
alongside `sysctl machdep.cpu` (`ARM processor`, `hw.cpufamily: 0`, `hw.ncpu: 4`) and `hw.optional.arm`.*

## How it works

```
 macOS processes (launchd, WindowServer, Safari...)    Linux processes (systemd, sshd, xnudrmd...)
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────    ────────────────────────────────────────────
 XNU (source-built, LINUX64 machine layer, kexts)  │
   ↕ linux64 host calls (xnu-patches/include/linux64_abi.h)
 xnu.ko   (APSL side: loads and runs the kernel collection)
   ↕ FKI, the foreign kernel interface (fki_*)
 fki.ko   (GPL side: CPUs, memory, faults, IPIs, files, network, host calls)
 Linux kernel (stock distro kernel, 4K pages, PAC)
```

- **CPUs**: each hosted CPU is a Linux kernel thread pinned to a Linux CPU. XNU runs on it until it calls the host
  (idle, I/O, a timer); Linux keeps its own exception vectors, and `fki.ko` forwards the faults and user exceptions of
  XNU code to XNU's handlers.
- **Memory**: XNU gets one physically contiguous block from Linux (CMA) and manages it with its own pmap; XNU and Linux
  share the user half of the address space layout (4K pages).
- **Devices**: kexts in `kexts/` give macOS a disk (a file on the Linux side), a display (a framebuffer Linux reads), a
  keyboard and pointer, an Ethernet link (a Linux network interface), a keystore and a GPU bridge.
- **GPU**: Metal in the hosted macOS runs on `gpu/xnu-cpu-metal` (metal2vulkan over Vulkan). Vulkan reaches the Linux
  host's GPU through the DRM bridge (`kexts/XnuDrm` → host call → `gpu/xnu-drm/xnudrmd` → the Linux render node), using
  Mesa's Venus driver; without a supported DRM bridge backend it falls back to Mesa lavapipe on the CPU.

## Status

Working on two arm64 Linux setups:

- **Apple Silicon Mac in an arm64 Linux VM (`krunkit`, 1 to 6 hosted CPUs)**:
  - macOS 27.2.1 boots to the desktop with auto-login in 31–48 s (an Apple Virtualization macOS VM on the same Mac:
    49 s).
  - Apps open and quit, Spotlight and the file system work; a 30-minute stress run (40 rounds of Safari, Notes,
    Calculator, TextEdit, System Settings, Spotlight and a disk walk) finishes with no panic and no crash report.
  - Runs as a systemd service: started at boot, stopped cleanly with the VM, restarted after a hosted-kernel panic, each
    run's log kept in `/var/log/xnulinux/`.
  - The GPU bridge gives hosted apps the host GPU (`Virtio-GPU Venus (Apple M5 Max)`) and is enabled by default
    (`GPU=auto`) when a virtio-gpu render node is present, falling back to CPU rendering (`GPU=off`) otherwise.
- **Bare-metal NVIDIA DGX Spark (Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS aarch64, Linux `7.0.0-1025-nvidia`)**:
  - Boots to the full macOS desktop (Screen Sharing and SSH working) directly on bare-metal arm64 Linux with `CPUS=4`
    and 8 GiB of RAM reserved for XNU.
  - Currently renders on the CPU (Mesa lavapipe, `GPU=off`): `xnudrmd` only forwards `virtio-gpu` (Venus) ioctls today,
    so hardware GPU pass-through on the GB10 GPU requires a new DRM bridge backend.

What is still a stopgap is listed in [`docs/production.md`](docs/production.md). Notably: the OS cryptex is merged into
the system volume, AMFI is patched and SIP relaxed, and memory access is slower than a native VM (4K pages vs 16K).

## Requirements

- An arm64 Linux host with PAC (`FEAT_PAuth`), 4K pages, and at least 16 GB of RAM (8 GB reserved for the hosted
  kernel). Tested on:
  - **NVIDIA DGX Spark** (bare-metal Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS aarch64, Linux `7.0.0-1025-nvidia`; CPU rendering for now).
  - **Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later)** running an arm64 Linux VM (`krunkit` for GPU access via virtio-gpu Venus, or
    `tart`).
- A Mac with Xcode to make the system disk and build the GPU parts.
- A macOS 27 installation (an Apple Virtualization VM disk) of your own. **No Apple binaries are in this repository or
  distributed by it**: the kexts Apple ships, the macOS system disk and its trust cache come from your own installation.

## Building and running

1. `scripts/vm-xnu-build.sh` (on the arm64 Linux host, once): sets up the macOS-DroidVM Linux toolchain and builds XNU
   (`xnu-12377.121.6`) natively on arm64.
2. `scripts/vm-xnu-rebuild.sh`: applies `xnu-patches/`, builds the kernel and `kexts/`, and links the kernel collection
   with Apple's kexts from your macOS installation.
3. `scripts/mk-macvm-disk.sh` (on the Mac): turns a macOS VM disk made by Apple's installer into the hosted system's disk
   and copies it into the Linux VM.
4. `scripts/xnulinux-boot.sh` (on the arm64 Linux host): builds `fki.ko` and `xnu.ko` against the running kernel, brings
   up the network (and the GPU bridge when there is a render node) and boots the hosted system. Its console is
   `scripts/xnu-console.sh`, its screen `tools/hosted/fb2png.py`, input `tools/hosted/xnu-input.py`. On a bare-metal
   host (such as a DGX Spark), set the carve-out (`mem=`, `carve_base=`, `carve_mb=`) to fit the machine's physical
   memory layout, and set `GPU=off` (`xnudrmd` supports only virtio-gpu for now).
5. `scripts/install-service.sh` (on the arm64 Linux host): runs it as `xnulinux.service`, configured in
   `/etc/xnulinux.conf` (CPUs, memory, disk, GPU). On the Mac, `scripts/install-krun-agent.sh` keeps the VM itself
   running.
6. GPU (optional, on the Mac): `gpu/venus/build-darwin.sh` builds the hosted Vulkan driver, `gpu/xnu-cpu-metal/` the
   Metal plugin (see its README).

## Repository layout and licenses

The Linux side and the XNU side are kept apart by license and meet only at FKI. Every source file carries an
`SPDX-License-Identifier`; the license texts are in [`LICENSES/`](LICENSES).

| Path | License | What |
|---|---|---|
| `fki-ko/`, `linux/` | GPL-2.0-only | FKI: the out-of-tree module for stock kernels, and the same as an in-tree driver |
| `xnu-ko/` | APSL-2.0 | `xnu.ko`: loads XNU's kernel collection and runs it; calls Linux only through `fki_*` |
| `xnu-patches/` | APSL-2.0 | The LINUX64 machine layer and the other changes to XNU's sources, and their shared headers |
| `kexts/` | APSL-2.0 | The hosted system's kexts (CPU, disk, keystore, Metal accelerator, DRM bridge) |
| `kexts/XnuDisplay/`, `kexts/XnuEthernet/`, `kexts/XnuInput/` | BSD-2-Clause-Patent | Derived from [macOS-DroidVM](https://github.com/Droid-VM/macOS-DroidVM)'s kexts |
| `gpu/xnu-cpu-metal/` | GPL-2.0-or-later | The Metal plugin over metal2vulkan (GPL-2.0-or-later); `XnuCpuMetalShim.h` is BSD-2-Clause-Patent (from [AdrenoMetal](https://github.com/UniXNU/AdrenoMetal)) |
| `gpu/xnu-drm/` | GPL-2.0-only, MIT | `xnudrmd` (the Linux end of the DRM bridge) is GPL; the protocol header and `darwin/` (built into Mesa) are MIT |
| `gpu/venus/` | GPL-2.0-only; patches MIT | Build scripts and tests; the patches to Mesa and virglrenderer are under their upstream license (MIT) |
| `gpu/xnu-cpu-metal/patches/` | upstream's | Patches to Mesa (MIT) and metal2vulkan (GPL-2.0-or-later) |
| `scripts/`, `tools/`, `tests/`, `docs/` | GPL-2.0-only | Build, disk, boot, debugging and test tools; documentation |

`xnu.ko` is on the XNU side of the line: it runs XNU's code in its own address space, so it is APSL-2.0 like XNU, and
Linux reports it as a non-GPL module (`MODULE_LICENSE("Proprietary")`, which taints the kernel as ZFS does). It must not
include Linux headers beyond the module ABI, call Linux functions other than `fki_*`, or carry Linux code. Upstream code
(XNU, macOS-DroidVM's toolchain, Mesa, metal2vulkan, the Vulkan loader, LLVM) is fetched at pinned revisions and patched at
build time; it is never committed.

## Acknowledgements

- [macOS-DroidVM](https://github.com/Droid-VM/macOS-DroidVM) and [UniXNU](https://github.com/UniXNU): the 4K-page XNU
  base, the Linux-hosted XNU toolchain, and the display, Ethernet and input kexts these are derived from.
- [metal2vulkan](https://github.com/steelbrain/metal2vulkan), [Mesa](https://mesa3d.org) (Venus, lavapipe),
  [virglrenderer](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/virgl/virglrenderer) and [krunkit](https://github.com/containers/krunkit).
- Apple's open-source XNU.

items.readme: # Xbox Emulator **Running the Xbox Series X|S library on PC. A continuation of [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox).** The runtime reimplements the console's platform layer (Xbox-flavoured Direct3D 12, precompiled RDNA2 shaders, unified-memory textures, system libraries) so dumped, already-decrypted Xbox Series X|S builds run as normal Windows processes. It is not tied to any single title. This repo tracks our continuation — new titles brought up, platform calls extended, shader stages unlocked. Uses legally obtained, already-decrypted dumps. The runtime does no key extraction or package decryption. **Source code:** the emulator's Rust workspace is in this repo: [`crates/`](crates/), [`tools/`](tools/) and `Cargo.toml`. It contains no game files, binaries or build output. **Contributing:** pull requests are welcome, especially console library functions still marked missing in the [library map](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. ## Status [![system functions](docs/img/badge-imports.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![Direct3D 12.x methods](docs/img/badge-d3d12x.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![RDNA2 instructions](docs/img/badge-instructions.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![shaders translated](docs/img/badge-shaders.svg)](#tested-titles) [![shader stages](docs/img/badge-stages.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![milestones](docs/img/badge-milestones.svg)](#milestones) [![titles examined](docs/img/badge-titles.svg)](#tested-titles) [![Xbox console libraries](docs/img/badge-console.svg)](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md) [![progress map](docs/img/progress.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) One square per item. The first four sections use upstream's definitions so the numbers stay comparable: green = done, amber = partial (a stub, a forwarder, or not verified to work), grey = not done — imported system functions of the Fortnite EXE, Direct3D 12.x interface methods, RDNA2 shader instructions the decoder knows, and the eight shader stages (mesh and amplification still grey). The fifth section is ours and covers Xbox console libraries only: the exports of the console OS DLLs (EmbeddedXvd of every analysed title, union, so the newest console OS sets the surface) that no same-named DLL in a PC's C:\Windows\System32 exports, so console-only DLLs (d3d12_xs, xg_xs, xmem, AcpHal, chad, xapu, xcrdapi, the *legacy variants, ...) count in full and modified PC DLLs (kernel32, advapi32, mfplat, ...) only for their console-only exports, plus the GDK wrappers the emulator redirects; plain Windows DLLs (ntdll, msvcrt, ucrtbase, combase, ...) are not shown. Coloured implemented / forwarded / stub / missing; lighter squares are functions an analysed title imports. Per-title import coverage likewise counts only imports from console libraries. Generated by tools/progress/gen.py; per-function tables in docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md, headline numbers in tools/progress/summary.json. ## Milestones Counted live by `tools/progress/gen.py`; full table with evidence in [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). | Milestone | State | |---|---| | All imported system functions covered (671/671) | done | | Full title shader sweep translated (105,506/105,506) | done | | All Direct3D 12.x methods covered | in progress (map) | | All RDNA2 instructions verified | in progress (map) | | All shader stages (Mesh, Amplification) | in progress (map) | | All Xbox console libraries covered | in progress (map) | | Fortnite boots, first frames, login, hotfix, mode select, BR lobby | done (7 run milestones) | | 3D scene correct | not reached | | Keyboard / controller input | not reached | | Audio | not reached | | Gameplay | not reached | | A second title running | not reached | ## Tested titles | Title | Build | Result | |---|---|---| | Fortnite (Chapter 2 Season 4) | 2.0.1461.7919 | Boots, logs in to a private server, reaches the lobby. 2D interface correct. 3D scene lit but the character material is wrong and bloom shows artifacts. No audio. Not playable. On this machine (2026-11-21): boots, first frames, window on the primary monitor, login complete, hotfix success, game-mode select, Battle Royale lobby (`UI.State.Athena.Frontend`). | | XDefiant | dump examined | **Not run.** Imports and console OS (10.0.22000) mapped in [docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md); new modules include XCurl, Bink2Scarlett, chad (XDsp*), xapu (XApu*). | | Grand Theft Auto VI | 1.0.2.1 | **Not run** (dump has no executable). items.readme:
# Xbox2Windows

Xbox2Windows researches static recompilation from Xbox Series X|S (Scarlett) to x64 Windows. It translates selected x64 machine code into C++ and selected gfx1013 shaders into desktop DXIL. The public tests build their own inputs and run without a game installation.

**Startup status.** Source-built Windows programs run from entry to process exit. The main executable was absent from the inspected package. Execution of the title's CPU code, full-game startup and frame rate remain unverified.

[Results](#current-results-and-open-work) · [Coverage chart](#instruction-coverage) · [Community and contributions](#community-and-contributions) · [Build on Windows](#first-build) · [Choose an experiment](#choose-an-experiment) · [Run the GPU check](#run-the-gpu-check)

## Current results and open work

| What runs | What was compared |
|---|---|
| **x64 programs from PE entry** | A two-record archive reader runs with blast 1.3 decompression under Windows, the PE mapper and the recompiled build. The three agree on output bytes, callback order, completed records, allocations, releases and exit status, including truncation and a refused output window. [Reproduce the archive comparison](docs/experiments.md#recompiling-the-blast-decoder) |
| **Raster draw from PE entry** | The shim-startup EXE renders the 64x64 test triangle offscreen. The native, mapped and recompiled runs agree on all 16,384 RGBA bytes and exit 42; a mirrored variant and an unknown draw case exercise the negative controls. [Reproduce the draw comparison](docs/experiments.md#exe-startup-through-the-desktop-runtime-shims) |
| **Pixel shaders** | At `c849f7a`, 851 of 12,101 PS records compiled, built D3D12 pipelines and matched controlled output on RTX 4060 Laptop and WARP. A two-mip draw verifies explicit LOD 0. A separate probe follows a constant-buffer read shared by 529 blocked records. Swapping buffers changes all 1,024 probe pixels. [Color readback](docs/experiments.md#offline-pixel-shader-recompilation) · [Depth and bindings](docs/experiments.md#buffered-depth-export) · [Read probe and latest counts](docs/experiments.md#first-unresolved-constant-buffer-read) |
| **Compute shaders** | Of 2,689 package records, 12 ran under the tested UAV bindings. Each adapter passed 14 full-buffer comparisons, including dispatches with different group counts. [Dispatch and readback](docs/experiments.md#compute-uav-stores-from-a-native-container) |
| **Mesh shaders** | A specialized entry fetched indexed vertices from a GPU buffer. Two position sets covered 1,024 and 276 pixels on a 32×32 target, matching the CPU reference on hardware and WARP. [Mesh draw and specialization limits](docs/experiments.md#single-group-mesh-entry-specialization) |
| **Windows runtime** | Bink frame-buffer allocations reach the Windows heap through the shared provider. The FidelityFX experiment follows scratch writes from two passes through the RCAS output on an 8×4 tile. [Allocation, failure and retry](docs/experiments.md#frame-buffers-through-the-shared-windows-heap) · [Upscaler pixel comparison](docs/experiments.md#last-writers-of-the-pass-26-scratch-reads) |

### Instruction coverage

The chart counts instruction forms exercised by passing source-built fixtures. The experiments above measure program outputs and package shader records.

![Instruction forms exercised by the latest published Windows CI fixtures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/refs/heads/coverage-dashboard/dashboard.svg)

Both Windows jobs on `main` must pass before CI publishes a new chart. The image shows the measured commit and run ID.

[Chart source commit and CI run](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/tree/coverage-dashboard#instruction-coverage) · [Find forms without a passing fixture](CONTRIBUTING.md#share-a-reproducible-finding)

## Community and contributions

- **Claim a task.** Search for the behavior or test name in [open issues](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues) and [open PRs](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pulls). On the issue, say what you will test, on which platform, and which shared interface or other PR your work depends on. For a first patch, start with [good first issues](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22).
- **Submit a change.** Keep the PR focused on one behavior. Link the task it advances and any prerequisite PR. Include the exact command, expected and observed results, and a negative control for a new fixture. [Patch and evidence guide](CONTRIBUTING.md#submit-and-review-a-patch)
- **Review a PR.** For CPU translation or PE loading, reproduce the comparison with the original fixture. For shaders or GPU compatibility, check the DXIL and relevant WARP or hardware results. Both reviewers cover shared CPU/GPU interfaces. Record your verdict and the commit you tested. The Maintainer merges after review threads are resolved and the required Windows check passes. [Review responsibilities](CONTRIBUTING.md#who-reviews-and-merges-a-pr)
- **Contribute a hardware result.** Run the [standalone GPU check](#run-the-gpu-check) and post the report in [issue #1](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1). You can also claim a batch there without owning a GPU. Verify the original logs, add new adapters as rows in the [hardware table](#hardware-coverage), and link driver retests in the existing row.

[New contributor guide](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/discussions/75) · [Build and debugging Q&A](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/discussions/categories/development-q-a) · [Report a bug or propose research](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/new/choose) · [Community conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) · [Private security reports](SECURITY.md)

## First build

On x64 Windows, install Python 3.11 or newer and Visual Studio's **Desktop development with C++** workload, including x64 MSVC, CMake, Ninja, and Windows SDK 10.0.26100 with DXC. Windows CI uses Python 3.12. Open PowerShell at the repository root and run the following commands.

```powershell
.\tools\dev.ps1
python -m venv out/pe-env
.\out\pe-env\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
cmake --preset dev
cmake --build --preset dev
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R 'desktop_root_signature|era_heap_allocation|offscreen_warp'
```

The smoke tests exercise a D3D12 root signature, heap allocation and software rendering. For just those checks, you can omit the two Python setup commands. With the Python environment installed, [run a focused experiment](#choose-an-experiment) or run the full suite with `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error`.

To build and test at /O2 as Windows CI also does, use the `release` preset in place of `dev`. Its build directory is `out/build/release`.

Contributing from macOS or Linux? See the [non-Windows host guide](docs/non-windows-hosts.md) for the platform-independent Python and LLVM 15 checks.

### Windows build notes

- **DXC validation.** `shader_metadata_probe` skips when the validator lacks module-only validation. DXC 1.8.2502 is the first verified release that passes. To use a separate DXC installation, configure with `cmake --preset dev -DDXC_EXECUTABLE=C:/path/to/dxc/bin/x64/dxc.exe`. [Results by release](docs/experiments.md#module-only-validation-by-dxc-release) · [Original report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/98) · [DXC download](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/releases/tag/v1.8.2502)
- **Windows 10.** The source-built BVH buffer operations run on in-box WARP at SM 6.0. For WARP checks that require SM 6.5 or DXR, use the app-local Agility SDK and WARP packages. [BVH buffer operations](docs/experiments.md#bvh-buffer-operations-on-in-box-warp) · [Windows 10 setup](docs/experiments.md#windows-10-with-the-app-local-agility-sdk-and-warp)
- **Independent build.** A Windows 11 contributor reproduced the three smoke tests from a clean checkout at `71bb9f4` and again after an incremental rebuild at `2465837`. [Toolchain, full-suite results and capability skips](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/2#issuecomment-7063351821)

## Choose an experiment

After the full [Windows build](#first-build), run one comparison from the repository root.

| Experiment | Focused test |
|---|---|
| Native, mapped and recompiled archive reader | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_archive_blast$' -V` |
| Indexed mesh draw on WARP | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_indexed_draw_warp$' -V` |
| Compute shader buffer writes on WARP | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_warp$' -V` |
| PE 32/64-bit base fixups against Windows | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_highlow$' -V` · [scope and controls](docs/experiments.md#highlow-and-mixed-width-base-relocations) |

The control-flow CPU translator supports [source-built string memory transfers](docs/experiments.md#string-memory-transfers-in-the-control-flow-cpu-lifter). MOVS and STOS, with and without REP, copy and fill 1-, 2-, 4- and 8-byte elements in either direction.

### Tests by area

| Area | A contribution you can verify | Focused CTest command |
|---|---|---|
| Static CPU recompilation | Compare leaf, chained-range and cross-function translations with their source-built originals and negative controls, including [Bink frame plane requests](docs/experiments.md#frame-plane-requests-in-binkallocateframebuffers) and the [Bink group descriptor builders](docs/experiments.md#grouped-allocation-descriptor-builders). | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_' -V` |
| Script states | Reproduce a parent/child lookup, an ambiguous selection or a damaged sibling link with a synthetic tree. | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^script_(state_literals\|path_links)$' -V` |
| Resource metadata | Check a [relocated resource root](docs/experiments.md#relocated-resource-root) against its block directory and type schema. | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^resource_relocated_root$' -V` |
| Texture recovery | Check a packed mip tail, a first refill byte, the fields of a generated BC7 block, or a resident mip drawn on the software adapter. [Look up a texture key across archives and inspect a matching descriptor](docs/experiments.md#reading-logical-ranges-and-probing-structured-resources). | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^(bcpack_prefix_and_mip_tail\|bc7_block_reference\|bc7_draw_warp\|resource_range_controls)$' -V` |
| Audio metadata | Inventory stream counts, codec IDs and sample rates in a bounded [AWC sound-effect bank](docs/experiments.md#awc-sound-effect-format-metadata). | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^audio_awc_metadata$' -V` |
| Compute shader recompilation | Translate fixed and indexed raw UAV stores, including an optional runtime constant buffer, and compare the complete buffer on D3D12. [Bindings and commands](docs/experiments.md#compute-uav-stores-from-a-native-container) | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_'` |
| Static shader recompilation | Translate pixel shader fixtures to desktop DXIL and check the output, including all 32 bits of an unsigned conversion. Select a local record by name and, for duplicate names, by decoded DXBC SHA-256. [Supported instructions and bindings](docs/experiments.md#offline-pixel-shader-recompilation) · [Float-to-uint readback and entry inputs](docs/experiments.md#unsigned-pixel-conversion-and-entry-inputs) | `ctest --preset dev -R '^pixel_aot_' -V` |
| Shader census | [Distinguish archive records, header digests and cache-index entries](docs/experiments.md#reporting-shader-census-populations) before choosing a coverage denominator. | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^shader_metadata_census$" -V` |
| Shader effect metadata | Inventory the [candidate programs for a named SGD5 effect](docs/experiments.md#candidate-programs-for-a-named-sgd5-effect) using independently located archive ranges. | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^sgd5_effect_candidates$" -V` |
| Pipeline readiness | Join explicit pipeline references to the native shader manifest and identify blockers for PSO creation. [Inputs and WARP control](docs/experiments.md#pipeline-readiness-from-shader-manifests) | `ctest --preset dev -R '^pso_' -V` |
| D3D12 and ray tracing | Compare the CPU reference, custom BVH shader and DXR on another adapter. Record the driver and native wave width. | `ctest --preset dev -R '^bvh_(differential\|wave64)_hardware$' -V` |
| Upscaler memory accounting | Compare [post-query counter writes](docs/experiments.md#upscaler-working-set-counter-updates) on success and failure. | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R 'working_set_delta$'` |
| Windows runtime | Add a source-built allocation case with a measurable Windows result. | `ctest --preset dev -R 'era_heap\|desktop_memory_query'` |
| PE tooling | Reproduce an import-resolution edge case with a DLL or EXE built from source. | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R 'static_exe_intake\|conditional_import_paths\|bundled_export_forwarders'` |
| Build and documentation | Try the first build from a clean clone. Identify the first missing prerequisite or unclear instruction. | Use the three-test command above. |

[Full experiment notes and reproduction commands](docs/experiments.md)

## Run the GPU check

Download the [Windows x64 GPU check and SHA-256](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/releases/tag/gpu-check-v0.1.0), verify and extract the ZIP, then run this in PowerShell from the extracted folder. The package contains its own shaders and needs no compiler, console or game files.

```powershell
.\Run-GpuCheck.ps1
```

With a package built from current source, use `.\Run-GpuCheck.ps1 -Adapter Radeon` to select a hardware adapter by part of its name. For source builds, set `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER` before running CTest.

Review `gpu-report-hardware.md` and paste its full contents as a comment on the [hardware coverage thread (#1)](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1). Do not open a new GitHub issue. Reports with a failure or capability skip are welcome. [Package instructions](tools/gpu-check/README.md)

items.name: nospeaker
items.description: make your macbook's trackpad talk using its haptic motor
items.readme:
```text
────────────────────────  a90.com presents  ─────────────────────────

    _   __ ____      _____  ____   ______ ___     __ __  ______ ____
   / | / // __ \    / ___/ / __ \ / ____//   |   / //_/ / ____// __ \
  /  |/ // / / /    \__ \ / /_/ // __/  / /| |  / ,<   / __/  / /_/ /
 / /|  // /_/ /    ___/ // ____// /___ / ___ | / /| | / /___ / _, _/
/_/ |_/ \____/    /____//_/    /_____//_/  |_|/_/ |_|/_____//_/ |_|

─  haptic voice synthesis  ─────────────────────────────  trackpad  ─
```

**Mute your Mac. Your trackpad will still talk.**

There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click.
NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it
into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger.

One command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used.

<!-- demo video: drag an .mp4 here in GitHub's editor -->

## 01 / before you start

```text
[ mute your mac ]        it still talks; that's the point
[ put it on a table ]    on your lap it's much quieter
[ hands off the glass ]  until it asks you to touch it
```

**Space** skips a part. **q** or **Ctrl-C** goes to the end.

## 02 / run it

`[ one line ]`

```sh
curl -fsSL a90.com/nospeaker | sh
```

Downloads the latest release to `~/.local/bin/nospeaker` and starts the show. `a90.com/nospeaker` points
to [play.sh](play.sh) in this repo, so you can read what it runs first.

`[ download ]`

Grab `nospeaker.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/os6/nospeaker/releases/latest),
unzip it and run `./nospeaker` in Terminal. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

`[ from source ]`

Needs Xcode or the Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`). Builds one program for Apple Silicon
and Intel Macs.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/os6/nospeaker
cd nospeaker
./build.sh
./nospeaker
```

## 03 / play with it

```text
./nospeaker "hello there"            say anything
./nospeaker --voice Daniel "hello"   in another macOS voice
./nospeaker --sweep                  a rising tone, 100 Hz to 4 kHz

--dark                               white on black
--plain                              no visuals, plain text
```

## 04 / needs

A Force Touch trackpad (built into MacBooks from 2015 on, or a Magic Trackpad 2 or newer), and macOS 12 or
later on Apple Silicon, or macOS 13 or later on Intel. Without a Force Touch trackpad, it says so and exits.

```text
tested on

MacBook Pro (Mac17,10)   M5 Max   macOS 27.2.1   everything works
```

Not tested yet: Intel Macs, a Magic Trackpad, and older versions of macOS. MultitouchSupport is private, so
older systems may lack the functions it uses, and loudness differs between trackpads. If you try it on another
Mac, open an issue with your model, your macOS version and how it sounded.

## 05 / how it works

```text
say ──▶ formants ──▶ two tones ──▶ motor ──▶ glass
        per 10 ms    F1 + F2       haptics   sound
```

**Why you can hear it.** The trackpad has no speaker, but the motor moves the glass. Driven back and forth
hundreds or thousands of times a second, the glass vibrates fast enough to make sound you can hear. It's quiet
because the motor is built for short taps, not for sound.

**The motor.** `MultitouchSupport` is the private framework macOS uses for the trackpad. Its function
`MTActuationCreateFromDictionary` takes a description of a vibration, a list of sine tones with a frequency,
a strength and a length each, and `MTActuationActuate` plays it on the motor. Apple's public haptics API only
offers three fixed taps.

**The range.** Measured with the MacBook's own microphone, every semitone from 98 Hz to 3,951 Hz: how loud it
is over a quiet room, and how much of the sound is the note itself.

```text
│                                      ###
│                          #+#     +++#####        #
│                         +#+#+   .+++#####       .#
│              .       ++++#+#+   .+++#####    # #.# #
│   ++        +. . #..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.###          .#
│   +++#.     +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+ #####.####+        .#
│  ++++#...   +...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+        .#
│ .++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+  +#    .#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#  .#.#
│..++++#...++++...+#..+++++#+#++++.+++#####+.#####.####+#.+#+..#.#
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      131         262         523         1047        2093    3951
   public notes stop at 600 Hz ─┘

across: every semitone, in Hz · up: loudness, +16 to +34 dB
# clean note   + fair   . mostly buzz
```

It's loud from about 100 Hz to 4 kHz, with a few dead spots where the glass resonates. Its loudest, cleanest
notes are around 1 kHz, which covers the most important part of a voice.

**The voice.** macOS's own voice speaks the line into memory. Every 10 ms, linear prediction finds the voice's
two strongest resonances (formants), its loudness and its pitch. The motor plays those two resonances as tones,
restarted on every beat of the pitch, so they buzz like a voice instead of whistling. Hiss sounds (s, f, t)
become quick bursts of high tones. Two resonances beat three: in a blind test they were clearer, and louder,
because the motor's strength is split fewer ways.

It sounds robotic, and it's much easier to follow when you can read along, which is why the show types every
line as it speaks.

**The code.** One Swift file, [nospeaker.swift](nospeaker.swift), with no dependencies.

## 06 / caveats

- **Is it safe?** It never drives the motor past its normal maximum strength. Going past it is possible and
  louder, but the driver starts to stall, so nospeaker doesn't.
- MultitouchSupport is private and undocumented, so a macOS update could break this.

The MultitouchSupport function names were learned from the open-source Tactile project. Everything else was
measured on a MacBook.

